extracted.intended_audience: depositors (inventors/assignees), patent attorneys/agents and depositary staff handling microorganism deposits under the Budapest Treaty
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and evaluative criteria for depositing biological materials (microorganisms, cell lines, plasmids, viruses, seeds, etc.) with international depositary authorities and national industrial property offices under the Budapest Treaty, including technical, administrative, availability, safety and fee requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storage and distribution of lyophilized material (NRRL)
rubrics_metrics.description: The NRRL stores and distributes lyophilized material supplied by the depositor if desired, or makes its own lyophilized preparations by subculture of, or directly from, active material supplied by the depositor; new batches are prepared as necessary for renewal of diminishing stocks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whichever method is used for preparing batches for distribution, NRRL stores a portion of the original prepared and deposited material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositor authenticity check and three-month reporting (NRRL)
rubrics_metrics.description: The NRRL requires the depositor to check the authenticity of its lyophilized preparations and record the result; if the depositor does not inform the NRRL of results within three months, NRRL assumes its preparations are equivalent to the depositor’s original deposit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The viability statement issued by the NRRL contains a section for the depositor to record authenticity check results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plasmid acceptance policy (NRRL)
rubrics_metrics.description: The NRRL does not accept plasmids, except when they are contained in a living host microorganism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official language requirement (NRRL/ATCC/NCMA)
rubrics_metrics.description: The official language of the depositary is English; communications in any other language are not accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is stated explicitly by NRRL, ATCC and NCMA.

rubrics_metrics.name: No written contract; depositor surrenders withdrawal right (NRRL/ATCC)
rubrics_metrics.description: The depositary does not enter into written contracts defining liabilities; by completing the deposition form the depositor surrenders any right to withdraw the deposit during required storage and accepts depositary policy and responsibility for authenticity of preparations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ATCC makes exception for certain dangerous organisms where depositor must agree to accept and handle at own risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Import/quarantine regulation responsibilities (NRRL/ATCC/NCMA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Import and/or quarantine regulations applicability varies: NRRL states such regulations do not apply to kinds accepted; ATCC must obtain import permits for cell lines and viruses and may require safety testing; NCMA typically not subject but depositor responsible if requirements apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors should contact depositary in advance for guidance on permits and testing; ATCC describes likely timelines and costs for USDA testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to complete depositary-specific Budapest Treaty deposition form (NRRL/ATCC/NCMA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Depositors are required to complete the depositary's Budapest Treaty deposition form (e.g., NRRL deposition form, ATCC BP/1, NCMA accession form) when making an original deposit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deposit-specific additional forms may be required for cell lines/viruses to enable import permits; later amendments or indications may use other specific forms (e.g., ATCC BP/7-8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Official notification forms for receipt and viability (BP/4, BP/9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Receipt and viability statements are issued on mandatory international forms BP/4 and BP/9 (sometimes combined as BP/4-9); notifications of furnishing to third parties use BP/14.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some depositaries (NRRL) modify BP/9 to include an authenticity check section; other official notifications may use depositary-specific forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unofficial early notification options (telephone/telex/fax) and fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Depositaires may, if requested, communicate deposit date and accession number or viability test results prior to issuing official forms; ATCC charges a fee (e.g., $10) for telephoning/faxing date of deposit and accession number, and will telephone viability results before official statement for a fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NRRL will telephone/telex date and accession number but not the viability result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supply of deposit certificates to patent agents
rubrics_metrics.description: If requested, depositaries will supply copies of the receipt and viability statement to the depositor’s patent attorney or agent; depositaries routinely ask for patent agent contact details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion of previous deposits to Budapest Treaty deposits (NRRL/ATCC/NCMA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies differ: NRRL does not permit conversion of deposits not originally made for patent purposes; ATCC permits conversion of deposits made outside Treaty provisions but charges storage fees on conversion (even if originally free); NCMA reports it does not have deposits outside Treaty provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative requirements for conversion generally mirror those for original deposits except fees or import/quarantine requirements may differ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements and acknowledgement for making a new deposit or replacement
rubrics_metrics.description: When making a new or replacement deposit after a deposit is found non-viable, depositaries may require an acknowledgment that the new deposit is the same as the original and may retain the initial deposit number and date if specified conditions are met (e.g., ATCC's three conditions: viability of replacement, receipt within three months of notification, and signed statement by depositor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental deposits (where characteristics change but deposit remains viable) obtain a new date and new accession number and pay regular fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositary preparation of distribution batches and depositor responsibility for stock renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: Some depositaries (NRRL, ATCC, NCMA) prepare additional samples for distribution from depositor material; for certain material types (viruses, plasmids, seeds, cell lines) the depositary may not prepare its own batches and the depositor is responsible for replenishing stock to ensure availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ATCC generally prepares additional samples for algae, bacteria, oncogenes, bacteriophages, yeasts, molds, and rarely cell lines/hybridomas; NCMA prepares own batches except where original deposit preserved by freezing/lyophilization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositor authentication check requirement (ATCC/NCMA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Depositors are required to test for authenticity of samples of all batches prepared by the depositary and to inform the depositary of the result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ATCC requires depositor to test authenticity and inform ATCC; NRRL similarly provides a section on the viability statement for depositor recording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kinds of microorganisms and biological material accepted (ATCC/NCMA lists)
rubrics_metrics.description: ATCC accepts a wide range: algae, animal viruses, animal cell cultures, bacteria (pathogenic and nonpathogenic), bacteriophages, embryos, DNA, fungi, human cell cultures, hybridomas, oncogenes, plant cell cultures, plant viruses, plasmids (in host and not in host), protozoa, RNA, seeds, yeasts; NCMA accepts algae, eukaryotic protists, bacteria, archaea or viruses from aquatic environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositor should contact depositary if material cannot be tested for viability in vitro or may require special permits for transport.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum acceptable biosafety containment level (ATCC)
rubrics_metrics.description: The highest acceptable containment level for deposits at ATCC is biosafety level (BSL) 3 as described in CDC/NIH biosafety publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors should consult CDC/NIH guidelines; some organisms may require additional handling/permits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and minimum quantity/replicates required for deposit (ATCC/NCMA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposited cultures are accepted in any form but depositaries prefer frozen or freeze-dried material and specify minimum numbers and volumes of replicates per material type (e.g., ATCC: 6 frozen/freeze-dried samples of microorganisms, 25 frozen samples of cell lines/hybridomas, 25 vials (100 ng) for plasmids, 2500 seeds etc; NCMA: minimum six replicates or duplicate 15 mL cultures for perpetual culturing and minimum cell/particle counts for algae, bacteria, viruses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exact minima depend on material type; consult depositary tables and contact depositary if uncertain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average time required for viability testing by material type (ATCC/NCMA)
rubrics_metrics.description: ATCC provides average viability testing times: bacteria 3-7 days, fungi 5-7 days, algae 10 days, cell lines 7-10 days, plasmids/phages 8-10 days, protozoa 10+ days, animal/plant viruses 30+ days, embryos and plant tissues variable. NCMA gives average 30 days for algae (up to 90) and up to 30 days for marine bacteria/archaea/viruses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deposit may take longer in some cases; depositors should expect variability and plan accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withholding samples for health and safety and requester competence
rubrics_metrics.description: Depositaires may withhold samples subject to health and safety regulations until the requesting party can comply; requesting party must be 'skilled in the art' before microorganisms are shipped, and for very dangerous organisms an assurance of acceptance of responsibility may be required; if organism produces restricted substances requestor must furnish registration numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overseas requesters are assumed to meet import requirements of their countries; depositary may advise if it knows specific import permit requirements elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of model request forms and advising on request procedures (NCMA/ATCC)
rubrics_metrics.description: NCMA will advise third parties of correct procedures and provide model request forms (BP/12) or national forms where supplied; ATCC will provide form BP/12 or forms used by individual offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NRRL generally does not advise third parties on procedures (except supplying EPO form when EPO regulations apply).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to depositor on furnishing of samples (BP/14 service)
rubrics_metrics.description: Depositaries notify the depositor on form BP/14 each time a sample of his deposit is furnished to a third party unless the depositor has waived the right to be notified; some depositaries offer BP/14 notification as a fee-based service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ATCC offers notification service for a fee; NRRL notifies unless waived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cataloguing policy for Budapest Treaty deposits
rubrics_metrics.description: Some depositaries (NRRL, NCMA) do not publish a catalog of Budapest Treaty deposits; ATCC lists an organism in its published catalog only if the depositor or a competent patent office instructs the ATCC to make samples available to anyone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositor can instruct depositary whether to list the organism publicly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule of fees (deposit and furnishing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposit and sample furnishing fees are charged and vary by depositary and material: NRRL example - deposit USD 500, furnishing USD 20; ATCC examples - storage & issuance of viability statement USD 2,500 per item, furnishing fees variable by biosafety level and recipient (ranges provided); NCMA lists storage and fees (e.g., frozen/lyophilized 30 years US$3,000, viability statement US$500, furnishing US$200).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees vary widely by institution, material, destination and hazard level; checks often must be in US dollars and institutional exemptions may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance materials and brochures
rubrics_metrics.description: Depositaires publish brochures, detailed statements on policies and procedures, and provide e-brochures or standard letters of explanation describing requirements and practices for patent-related deposits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors are encouraged to request guidance documents from the depositary in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of samples relative to patent/prosecution timeline (ATCC/NCMA/Australia)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally, availability is required only after issuance of a pertinent patent; prior to that time a deposit need only be made available if a patent office issues a decision to release the deposit, another contracting patent office issues such decision, or the original depositor requests release to a particular requesting party. In Australia, samples may be made available once the specification is open to public inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants in some jurisdictions can limit availability to specified periods or nominate who may receive samples before publication/grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requestor undertakings and restrictions on use (Australia/Austria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requesting parties may be required to give undertakings not to make the microorganism or derived cultures available to others and to use the microorganism only for experimental purposes in relation to specified proceedings (e.g., opposition), and may be required to provide security for damages for breaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some jurisdictions permit applicants to restrict availability before publication or require samples only be provided to an independent expert.

rubrics_metrics.name: National industrial property office requirement to deposit (country-specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: Industrial property offices specify whether deposit with an international depositary authority is obligatory to describe the invention adequately (examples: Australia requires deposit when microorganism not reasonably available and necessary to perform the invention; Austria requires deposit if biological material not accessible or cannot be described sufficiently).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory references: Australia Patents Act 1990 sections and regulations; Austria Patent Act Section 87a; check national law for exact triggers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time of deposit relative to filing/priority (national offices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Most national offices require deposit on or before the filing date of the application and, where priority is claimed, on or before the priority date (e.g., Australia, Armenia, Austria).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some offices allow later filing of deposit-related information within specified windows (e.g., Austria allows certain information within 16 months or other events).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of storage by depositary / statutory minimums
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposit duration rules: Australia - store at least five years after most recent request and at least 30 years after deposit; NCMA/ATCC/NRRL typically store for 30 years for patent cultures (sometimes longer depending on arrangement or perpetual culturing options); Armenia requires storage guaranteeing protection at least during the viability period of the patent; some offices list 'no provision.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check specific depositary and national rules for exact storage terms and special cases (perpetual culturing vs frozen/lyophilized).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for furnishing samples: who may request and when (national offices)
rubrics_metrics.description: National offices define when samples should be available (e.g., Australia: when specification is open to public inspection; Austria: before publication persons with right of inspection; from publication any requester).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access may be subject to obligations and conditions imposed by law or the depositary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on availability after refusal/withdrawal (Armenia/Austria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent application is refused or withdrawn, some national rules permit the deposited biological material to be available to third parties for a specified period (e.g., Armenia: 20 years from filing if so requested; Austria: availability until grant or, if withdrawn or rejected, for 20 years from application date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check national law for precise durations and conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent expert hand-out option prior to publication (Austria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Until completion of technical preparation for publication, the applicant may request that access be granted only by handing a sample to an independent expert rather than to the requesting party directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The independent expert is governed by statutory definitions and obligations; this protects confidential technical preparation phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant control over pre-publication availability (Australia)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may notify the Commissioner that a sample is only to be provided during specified periods (e.g., before grant or before the application has lapsed/been withdrawn/refused to a nominated skilled addressee without interest in the invention).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows applicants to limit pre-publication dissemination subject to national regulations.
